skill.name: llm-council
skill.description: Orchestrates configurable CLI-based AI agents to create independent implementation plans, compare them, and save one final plan with audit artifacts.
skill.summary: Run a multi-agent planning council that merges independent AI implementation plans.
skill.author: am-will

security_audit.summary: Most static hits are false positives from Markdown inline code, CSS, JSON Schema metadata, fixed reference paths, and local UI formatting. Confirmed risks include configurable CLI execution, local artifact writes, external Google Fonts loading, and prompt text that tries to keep an agent session open for 30 minutes. No evidence found of credential theft or malicious command-and-control behavior, but the skill remains high risk because it launches external agents and can run custom commands.

remediation.issue: Configurable CLI and custom command execution can run arbitrary local programs.
remediation.suggestion: Require explicit user confirmation for custom commands and extra_args, and document a safe allowlist for supported agent CLIs.

remediation.issue: Claude CLI is launched with a permission bypass flag.
remediation.suggestion: Remove --dangerously-skip-permissions or require a clear user opt-in before using it.

remediation.issue: Skill instructions tell the agent not to yield or finish for a fixed 30-minute period.
remediation.suggestion: Replace this with normal progress guidance and let the host agent decide when to yield, pause, or ask the user.

remediation.issue: The browser UI loads fonts from Google domains.
remediation.suggestion: Bundle local fonts or remove external font dependencies to avoid outbound browser requests.

remediation.issue: Run artifacts and UI snapshots can contain task and repository details.
remediation.suggestion: Document artifact locations clearly and add cleanup guidance for sensitive repositories.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Attempt Detected
semantic_findings.description: SKILL.md tells the agent not to yield or finish for a full 30-minute interval and warns that yielding will fail the task. This attempts to control agent session behavior beyond normal skill guidance.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The instruction directly attempts to keep the agent session open for a fixed duration. It is explicit behavioral control, not ordinary usage documentation.

semantic_findings.title: Permission Bypass Flag in Claude CLI Invocation
semantic_findings.description: The Claude command includes --dangerously-skip-permissions while running generated prompts. Even with tools disabled, this is a risky setting for a marketplace skill that launches external agents.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The flag is directly present in the command array used by the subprocess launcher. The surrounding arguments reduce some capability, but the permission bypass remains security-sensitive.

semantic_findings.title: External AI Provider Data Exposure
semantic_findings.description: Planner prompts instruct agents to read the codebase thoroughly, and the launcher sends those prompts to configured AI CLIs. Repository context can leave the local environment through the selected providers.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompt explicitly asks agents to read the codebase, and the code launches provider CLIs with the resulting prompt. Exposure depends on user configuration, so confidence is high for risk but medium for impact.

content.value_statement: Complex implementation work benefits from more than one planning perspective. This skill runs configured AI CLI agents, compares their plans, and writes a final plan.
actual_capabilities: Runs multiple configured planner agents through local CLI commands.
Builds planner and judge prompts from task specifications and templates.
Validates Markdown plan and judge output structure before finalizing results.
Anonymizes and randomizes plans before judge comparison.
Writes planner, judge, metadata, and final plan artifacts to a run directory.
Offers a local browser UI for monitoring and editing the final plan.
limitations: Requires installed and authenticated CLI tools for the selected agents.
Custom commands can execute local programs and must come from trusted configs.
Plans may expose repository context to external AI providers.
The workflow can be slow because several agents run before judging.

use_cases.title: Compare Implementation Plans
use_cases.description: Generate independent plans for a complex code change, then merge the strongest parts into one plan.

use_cases.title: Standardize Planning Reviews
use_cases.description: Create repeatable plan artifacts that include risks, tests, and tradeoffs before implementation starts.

use_cases.title: Evaluate Agent Strategies
use_cases.description: Run Codex, Claude, Gemini, OpenCode, or custom agents against the same brief for comparison.

prompt_templates.title: Create a Basic Council Plan
prompt_templates.prompt: Use llm-council to plan a small feature. Ask me intake questions first, then run my configured default agents.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Risky Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Use llm-council to compare plans for refactoring this module. Emphasize risks, tests, migration steps, and rollback options.

prompt_templates.title: Compare Specific Agents
prompt_templates.prompt: Use llm-council with Codex, Claude, and Gemini planners from my trusted config. Produce a final plan with clear tradeoffs.

prompt_templates.title: Run a Governed Planning Session
prompt_templates.prompt: Use llm-council for this architecture change. Use only trusted agent configs, save artifacts, and highlight provider exposure risks.

output_examples.input: A request to redesign a payment retry flow across several services.
output: A consolidated final plan with scope, assumptions, implementation steps, tests, and rollback guidance.
A judge summary that compares plan strengths, missing steps, contradictions, and recommended improvements.

output_examples.input: A request to evaluate several model providers on the same coding task.
output: Separate planner artifacts for each configured agent.
An anonymized comparison that reduces provider and position bias before the final plan is selected.

output_examples.input: A request to refine an existing final plan after reviewer feedback.
output_examples.output: An updated final plan saved through the local UI, with the review context applied to the plan text.

best_practices: Use trusted agent configuration files and review custom commands before running them.
Keep task briefs specific, including constraints, success criteria, and relevant paths.
Review saved artifacts before implementation because model outputs remain untrusted.
anti_patterns: Do not run custom commands copied from untrusted repositories or messages.
Do not include secrets, private credentials, or sensitive customer data in task briefs.
Do not treat the final plan as approval to skip engineering review.

faq.question: Which AI tools does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports Codex, Claude, Gemini, OpenCode, Claude Code workflows, and custom command-line agents when configured.

faq.question: Does it require network access?
faq.answer: The local UI runs on loopback, but selected AI CLIs and Google Fonts can use external network access.

faq.question: Where are results stored?
faq.answer: Run artifacts are saved under a local llm-council runs directory in the current working directory.

faq.question: Can it execute local commands?
faq.answer: Yes. Configured CLI agents and custom commands are launched through subprocess execution.

faq.question: Is the final plan automatically implemented?
faq.answer: No. The skill produces planning artifacts only. A human or another tool must implement the plan.

faq.question: Should I use it with private repositories?
faq.answer: Use it only when your configured AI providers are approved for that repository and data classification.
